OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode

OpenCode Community Digest — 2026-11-03

1. Today's Highlights

No releases in the last 24 hours, but issue activity is dominated by free-tier quota problems (the mega-thread #59387 now sits at 230 comments) and a wave of Companion/Desktop stability reports (local server startup failures, IPC errors, and stale background services). On the engineering side, several well-scoped fixes landed targeting compaction behavior, SSE keepalive handling, and session terminal shell resolution, while multiple i18n/ecosystem doc PRs continue to flow in from contributors.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24h.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #59387 — Free tier issues: read this first, then post your report here (230 comments, 👍 17) The central clearinghouse for free-tier complaints: quota-exceeded errors, reset times that never arrive, and Desktop builds refusing to run. This is the single highest-signal thread for gauging free-tier sentiment.

  2. #61346 — [reproduced] compaction: stuck on "Compacting" with no feedback when provider fails or sends only SSE keepalives A /compact sat for 90+ minutes with no error while upstream returned 503 no eligible upstream account. Breaks the retry/notice UX and required manual interrupt to recover.

  3. #61072 — Claude Agent: 5-hour plan limit drains ~1.8x faster because SDK labels requests sdk-ts A measurable cost regression for Claude Agent users — the Agent SDK entrypoint label appears to affect quota accounting, making OpenCode ~1.8x more expensive than Claude Code's own TUI for the same work.

  4. #61371 — core: transcript shortening clips every tool output in an exchange at once, leaving most of the window unused A compaction algorithm flaw: flattenAndDropOldest operates per-exchange, so a long post-checkpoint exchange gets truncated wholesale rather than proportionally. Inefficient context use with real token cost implications.

  5. #50633 — feature(desktop): system tray icon with clean shutdown of background opencode-cli service (Windows) (9 comments, 👍 4) The spawned opencode-cli.exe outlives the Desktop window and keeps a stale config loaded. A long-lived request with sustained 👍 indicating real desktop friction.

  6. #51051 — [reproduced] session terminal ignores the shell config option (always PowerShell on Windows) Documented behavior diverges from implementation: the agent's shell tool respects shell, session terminals only read process.env.SHELL (unset on Windows). A clean, fixable config/implementation gap.

  7. #61363 — Bug: TUI intermittently unresponsive on fresh launch with background server Intermittent startup hang tied to background server boot. Combined with #61357 and #61226, this forms a cluster of "fresh launch is flaky" reports.

  8. #61357 — An error occurred while starting the local server (Desktop IPC handler failed) Desktop-side IPC failure surfacing during local server startup. Symptom-level, but part of the broader Desktop reliability theme.

  9. #61232 — provider(opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash): user message starting with an absolute file path always fails with empty response + auto-retry Deterministic provider bug: messages beginning with an absolute path never reach the model. Highly reproducible and worth watching for a quick fix.

  10. #54863 — [FEATURE]: Indexed cross-session transcript search in the V2 SDK (SQLite FTS5) (👍 1) session.list({ search }) only matches titles; finding sessions by content requires full scans. Relevant to SDK consumers building bots (e.g., Kimaki) and a sensible long-term platform improvement.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #61376 [CLOSED] — fix(ai): don't let SSE keepalives reset the chunk timeout Directly addresses the compaction stall in #61346 (keepalive half). Prevents SSE keepalives from indefinitely extending the chunk timeout.

  2. #61353 — fix(server): resolve the configured shell for session terminals Fixes #51051 by routing session terminals through the configured shell instead of process.env.SHELL.

  3. #55208 — fix: Rehook compaction Rebuilds reduced drafts before rerunning compaction hooks, so shrinking no longer restores checkpoint text a request hook removed. Closes #54916.

  4. #61360 — fix(opencode): cancel pending tool approvals with their owner Cancelling a V1 session now ends its tool permission wait and removes the stale approval card — a real UX correctness fix for interrupted sessions.

  5. #61351 [CLOSED] — fix(ai): ignore tool-call deltas arriving after finish_reason Hardens the OpenAI Chat parser against non-compliant routers (e.g., Poe) that stream tool-call chunks after finish — previously crashed the session with InvalidProviderOutput.

  6. #58492 [CLOSED] — fix(core): never let compaction ceiling exceed the output reservation Fixes inverted ceilings on large-window models by capping the compaction ceiling relative to the output reservation.

  7. #59707 — fix(core): log skipped plugin discovery Addresses silent plugin-dir drops (including the NixOS/home-manager symlink case) — diagnostics for a recurring configuration mystery.

  8. #59528 — fix(core): drop a well-known source when its last credential is removed opencode auth logout now cleans up the .well-known/opencode source so it doesn't fall back to stale state.

  9. #55484 — feat(core): add scrape.do web search provider Adds a new web search backend — evidence that the search-provider surface keeps expanding.

  10. #57358 — fix(app): keep local sessions in the selected directory Prevents local sessions from escaping the selected directory (refs #51191, addresses #51992). Important for multi-project workflows.

5. Hot Discussions

No dedicated Discussion data was provided; this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Localization / i18n: Multiple PRs (#61361, #61366) target Russian UI and TUI localization, continuing long-running refs (#37216, #50164).
  • Desktop lifecycle & service management: System tray + clean background-service shutdown (#50633); GUI plugins loading in the web app (#60976).
  • Context / compaction transparency: Per-turn context drift inspector (#58459) and per-session Go allowance persistence (#59653).
  • SDK observability/search: SQLite FTS5 indexed transcript search (#54863).
  • Session management UX: Delete sessions from the TUI (#26056) — a long-standing, low-friction request.
  • Ecosystem expansion: New Telegram and QQ bot channel plugins (#59301, #61355).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Free-tier quota accounting is the top complaint — reset times not working, "used today's free messages" on first request, and Desktop refusing to launch for free users. The 230-comment thread (#59387) plus multiple duplicates (#61222, #61375) signal a genuine bug and a support-backlog problem.
  • Compaction is a recurring fault line: stalls with no feedback on provider failure (#61346), inefficient per-exchange truncation (#61371), and ceiling inversion on large-window models (#58492). Also a reported regression in context efficiency for "Big Pickle" (#61352).
  • Desktop/TUI startup reliability: stale background services, IPC failures, and intermittent startup hangs (#50633, #61357, #61226, #61363, #60854) produce a cluster of "fresh launch is flaky" reports.
  • Hidden cost regressions: Claude Agent quota draining ~1.8x faster (#61072) erodes trust in provider integration accounting.
  • Config options silently ignored: shell (#51051) and plugin discovery symlinks (#59707) — configuration that appears valid but isn't honored.
  • Provider edge-case crashes: empty responses on path-prefixed messages (#61232), post-finish tool deltas (#61351), and scope errors after upgrades (#61342) point to brittleness in the provider layer.

Note: Commentary is based solely on the provided issue/PR metadata (titles, summaries, counts); no external verification was performed.

Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-11-03

1. Today's Highlights

Pi v1.5.0 shipped with visible extension changelogs on fresh launches. Meanwhile, a regression in 0.99.x around terminal color query replies (mintty/ConPTY) remains the most active issue this cycle, and a cluster of schema-resolution, context-budget, and RPC lifecycle fixes landed via bot-authored PRs.

2. Releases

v1.5.0 — New Features

  • Extension update changelogs: after updating installed extension packages, the next fresh launch shows what changed. Package authors can choose the changelog path, and collapseChangelog condenses the notices.
  • Link: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/releases

3. Hot Issues

  1. #10256 [OPEN] [bug, inprogress] Terminal color query replies leak into prompt; BEL opens external editor (mintty/ConPTY) — 21 comments, 👍4. Regression between 0.87.1 (fine) and 0.99.x; startup emits raw color-query escape sequences into the prompt. High-impact for Windows mintty users. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10256
  2. #10497 [CLOSED] [bug] OpenRouter Error: 400 — 15 comments. Context-length overruns when extensions inject file contents; points to token-budget accounting gaps with OpenRouter's stricter pre-routing checks. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10497
  3. #10605 [OPEN] [bug] ChatGPT/OpenAI OAuth 403 — 12 comments. "ChatGPT user is not eligible for subscription sharing" blocks Plus-tier OAuth users even after re-login. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10605
  4. #10956 [OPEN] cacheWarming "idle" stops silently after turn_end + custom/compaction message — 11 comments, 👍2. Idle cache warming never fires (Inactive (conversation context changed)); affects cost/latency for long sessions. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10956
  5. #10470 [OPEN] RPC new_session/switch_session/fork/clone emit session_start twice — 8 comments. Duplicate lifecycle events break extension state machines in RPC mode. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10470
  6. #11021 [OPEN] ChatGPT sign-in uses 272K context for gpt-6.1-sol despite 500K catalog — 7 comments, 👍7. Undersized context budget triggers premature compaction; strong community agreement. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11021
  7. #11599 [OPEN] RPC: async ctx.shutdown() does not exit idle process — 5 comments. Headless/RPC embedders see hung processes on async shutdown. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11599
  8. #9276 [OPEN] [bug, inprogress] grep tool with context lines can cause OOM — 4 comments. Reading whole matched files for context lines caused heap exhaustion in headless SDK use. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9276
  9. #11697 [OPEN] [fix-available] Relative $id resolved twice breaks tool arg validation — 3 comments. Valid tool arguments rejected when schemas use relative $id + local $ref. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11697
  10. #11699 [OPEN] Remove tool truncation in codemode — 1 comment. Request to let codemode chain tools without truncation, since truncation defeats its main value. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11699

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #11726 [OPEN] fix(schema): apply relative root $id only once when resolving references — Fixes double-resolution of relative root $id that broke local $refs (paired with issue #11697). https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11726
  2. #11725 [CLOSED] fix(ai): remove Codex SSE retry abort listener after backoff — Prevents abort-listener leaks accumulating per retry in the Codex Responses provider. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11725
  3. #11724 [CLOSED] fix(mcp): clean up server children on stdio close after server exited — Ensures orphaned child processes in the MCP process group are killed even when the parent already exited. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11724
  4. #11705 [OPEN] fix(coding-agent): take grep context from ripgrep instead of reading matched files — Direct fix for the OOM in #9276; memory now scales with output, not file size. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11705
  5. #11545 [OPEN] Anthropic message threads — Uses Anthropic's server-side message threads beta, sending only new messages when caching is on; still falls back to full requests on mismatch. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11545
  6. #11712 [CLOSED] [inprogress] fix(ai): leave room for OpenRouter input overcount when clamping max tokens — Addresses OpenRouter's stricter tokenizer (up to ~12% overcount) causing 400s for near-window models. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11712
  7. #11709 [CLOSED] fix(coding-agent): report installed version after npm/pnpm/yarn/bun self-update — Stops claiming an update succeeded when the package manager actually reinstalled the old version. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11709
  8. #11707 [CLOSED] feat(coding-agent): list updated packages with version changes in pi update — Makes pi update output show which extensions changed and to what version. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11707
  9. #11629 [CLOSED] feat(coding-agent): add PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND and selfUpdateCommand — Lets wrapper-managed installs (mise, nub, Nix) define how pi update should update Pi. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11629
  10. #11686 [OPEN] feat: release version tags on pkg.earendil.com — Fixes release pipeline so tagged release commits are actually built (v1.2.0–v1.4.0 had no builds). https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11686

5. Hot Discussions

Ideas

  • #4444 Supporting the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) — 5 comments, 👍47 (highest-engagement item this cycle). Proposal to replace pi-specific RPC with a standard agent↔editor protocol so every editor doesn't need a bespoke client. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/discussions/4444

Q&A

  • #11404 Official Pi code agent sandbox by Docker? — 2 comments, 👍2. User found sbx/pi, sbx/pi-mixin, sbx/pi-image, and sbx/pi-kit images on Docker Hub and asks whether they're official. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/discussions/11404

Show and tell

  • #11722 OnlyClaws Android — give Pi a phone claw (live wallpaper, overlay, TTS via js) — A thin Android host running agent-pushed JS (Rhino + A2UI + transparent WebView overlay + TTS), echoing the low-cost-device agent pattern. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/discussions/11722

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Standardized editor integration: ACP support (#4444, 👍47) is the clearest signal that embedders want a protocol, not a custom RPC dialect.
  • Observability / determinism in extension machinery: --print-skills / pi skills (#11700), exporting VIRTUAL_MODULES for embedders (#11727), and a settings-level skill prune control (#11701) all ask for inspectable, deterministic behavior instead of model-mediated output.
  • Extension capability expansion: invoking registered/MCP tools from event hooks (#10264), background-job-aware status (#11702), and disabling built-in truncation in codemode (#11699).
  • Update/install UX: package-level changelogs (shipped in v1.5.0), per-package version reporting (#11707), accurate post-update versions (#11709), and wrapper-defined self-update (#11629).
  • Session management: hiding child sessions in /resume (#9847) and cross-restart durability (#11635).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Context/token accounting mismatches: OpenRouter's pre-routing tokenizer overcount (#10497, #11712) and ChatGPT OAuth reporting 272K instead of 500K (#11021) both produce 400s or premature compaction.
  • Headless/RPC mode rough edges: duplicate session_start events (#10470), async ctx.shutdown() hangs (#11599), and extensions silently losing turns in -p/--mode json (#11011).
  • Memory safety in tools: grep with context lines reading whole files caused production OOM in SDK use (#9276, PR #11705).
  • Silent failures: length recovery dropping replies with exit 0 (#11012), image-only steer poisoning every subsequent request with empty text blocks (#11728), and extension-registered models crashing calculateCost (#10209).
  • Update-reliability trust: stale registry metadata making pi update claim success while reinstalling old versions (#11707, #11709), and unsupported self-update paths for wrapper-managed installs.
  • Terminal/platform compatibility: the 0.99.x mintty/ConPTY escape-sequence regression (#10256) and WSL clipboard history gaps (#6003) remain recurring Windows-adjacent friction.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-03

1. Today's Highlights

The project shipped v0.26.6 alongside TypeScript SDK v0.1.27, headlined by a new Web Shell sidebar activity view for trusted workspaces and a batch of Anthropic provider timeout and transport fixes. CI health remains the dominant operational concern: long-running bot-generated failure issues (#14724 at 161 comments, #13078 at 40) are still accumulating, and a new P1 reports that bot workflow bursts are exhausting the GITHUB_TOKEN rate limit and breaking unrelated CI jobs. Meanwhile, session-state durability (SIGHUP losses, unrecorded tool results) and model-ID normalization bugs across Bedrock/OpenRouter/Ollama surfaced as active themes.

2. Releases

CLI v0.26.6

  • New: Web Shell sidebar activity view for trusted workspace conversations, surfacing approval/input/error states and unread counts.
  • No known breaking changes.
  • Nightly v0.26.5-nightly.20261102.0441faff21 also published.

SDK TypeScript v0.1.27

  • Bundles CLI 0.26.6 (built from the same branch/ref as the SDK).

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate, no test identified (161 comments, open since 2026-10-19). The longest-running bot-filed CI failure thread; the lack of an identified test suggests a flaky or infrastructure-level gate rather than a code regression. High comment volume signals repeated re-triggering without resolution.

  2. #13078 — Daily dependency CVE audit failed (40 comments). A month-old, still-open security-hygiene failure. Persistent audit failures erode trust in the supply chain signal and are likely blocked on the npm audit endpoint or a genuine high-severity finding.

  3. #16169 — Queued messages silently lost on SIGHUP (P2). A message typed while a tool runs is held in the queue (footer shows ⏳ 1 queued), then vanishes entirely on terminal close — not in the resumed conversation, not in any file. A clear data-loss UX bug with fresh community attention.

  4. #15799 — Completed tool calls reported as "not recorded … Treat as failure and retry" (P1). In-flight calls during abrupt session end are misclassified on resume. Same family as #16169: session durability under interruption is a recurring correctness gap.

  5. #16144 — Web Shell GitHub/GitLab channels start open to anyone (P1, security). Channels created from Web Shell default to Open group policy, contradicting docs that say group access is disabled by default — a security-relevant default mismatch.

  6. #16188 — Bot workflow burst exhausts GITHUB_TOKEN rate limit (P1). Four CI jobs on PR #16182 failed with HTTP 403 due to autofix/triage/review bot bursts. Directly impacts contributor velocity.

  7. #16171 — Web Shell session open very slow: live replay retains full file contents from edit tool results (P1, closed). Daemon resources normal; the slowdown is replay-payload bloat. Quickly closed, but highlights growing pains in Web Shell session scaling.

  8. #15165 — Shell safety parser triggers ~1.6 GiB transient WASM allocation on Node 24.16.0 (P2, performance). Measured native-memory spike during V8 optimization of the bundled Bash WASM parser — a serious footprint concern for constrained environments.

  9. #16157 / #16158 / #16159 — Model IDs lose context/output limits (Bedrock, OpenRouter :exacto, Ollama HF quant tags). A coordinated trio from one reporter: normalization reduces IDs to garbage, silently falling back to 200K/32K defaults. Same root cause class across three providers.

  10. #16127 — VS Code Companion 0.26.5 SIGSEGV decoding images with Sharp under Electron-as-Node (P1, Linux). Crash-on-image-decode is a hard blocker for IDE users; complements #16063 (Generated UI MCP server spawned as Electron GUI instead of Node), suggesting a broader Electron runtime-mode issue cluster.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #16177 — fix(core): attribute monitor and workflow notifications to the registering turn. Fixes background results arriving as a new turn instead of being included in the active turn's next model request — the server-side counterpart to Web Shell issue #16119.

  2. #16193 — fix(core): honor Anthropic transport timeout configuration (closed/merged). Passes the selected Undici dispatcher through the custom fetch; directly addresses #16187's 300s timeout despite configured longer timeouts.

  3. #16199 — fix(serve): address remote-access review findings R1-6/7/9/11. Follow-up to #15887, which merged with 17 unresolved review threads; this lands four verified functional/security fixes.

  4. #16023 — feat(managed-agent): share resident external Workspace across sessions. Reuses a Workspace-scoped worker binding across Sessions/Turns instead of teardown per cycle — a meaningful efficiency change for managed agents.

  5. #16201 — feat(managed-agent): enforce row integrity for governed SQL catalogs. Proposes governance for the 39-table resident Workspace stack, moving 73 CHECK predicates into complete-row Java validation.

  6. #16064 — fix(cli): run bundled generated-ui server in Node mode under Electron. Pins ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 for the stdio spawn path — the fix for the #16063 class of bugs.

  7. #16117 — feat(channels): deliver GitHub events to PR-bound sessions. Routes PR events (created/reviewed/verified bindings) into the owning session as prompts — a step toward event-driven agent workflows.

  8. #16149 — feat(web-shell): edit GitHub repository settings from the channel editor. Exposes account allowlists, no-@mention answering, and related policies in UI instead of hand-editing settings.json — relevant to the #16144 security-default discussion.

  9. #16105 — feat(serve): configurable Conversations working-directory root. Adds --conversations-dir / QWEN_CONVERSATIONS_DIR for qwen serve and qwen daemon start, with explicit precedence over environment.

  10. #16190 (closed) / #16192 (closed) — unified agent loop rollout. ACP cron/background-notification turns now run on the shared loop (PR 2c-4, last ACP turn kind), and the nightly E2E lane gains a QWEN_CODE_ENABLE_UNIFIED_AGENT_LOOP=1 leg — signals the default flip is approaching (#15327).

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussion data was provided in this dataset; section omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Fine-grained content referencing for token efficiency — #16173 asks for models to reference slices of files/tool outputs instead of duplicating them, targeting the read > write > typo > re-write loop. Fits the roadmap/context-performance theme.
  • Configuration control for managed/privacy-sensitive installs — #16006 (closed) requested disabling the daily models.dev catalog refresh from settings, honoring privacy opt-outs.
  • Desktop distribution breadth — #16034 (closed) requests rpm artifacts for Fedora/RHEL (currently AppImage-only, which cannot install), with an inline patch supplied.
  • Web Shell as a configuration surface — multiple PRs (#16149) and issues point toward moving channel/repo policy out of settings.json and into UI.
  • Background automation semantics — notification attribution (#16177/#16119) and PR-bound event delivery (#16117) indicate demand for agents that react mid-turn and to external events.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. Session-state durability under interruption — The strongest recurring cluster: queued messages lost on SIGHUP (#16169), completed calls misreported as failures after abrupt ends (#15799), and unrecorded-result messaging that forces retries. Users lose work and trust in resume semantics.
  2. CI signal noise and self-inflicted outages — Bot-filed mega-threads (#14724, #13078, #15173, #12714) plus token-rate-limit exhaustion (#16188) mean CI failures are increasingly infrastructure/bot-driven, drowning real regressions and blocking unrelated PRs.
  3. Model-ID normalization is silently wrong — A single reporter filed Bedrock (#16157), OpenRouter :exacto (#16158), and Ollama HF quant-tag (#16159) variants in one day; all silently fall back to default 200K/32K limits, causing wrong context budgeting with no warning.
  4. Electron runtime-mode bugs in the VS Code companion — Generated UI MCP server launched as GUI instead of Node (#16063) and Sharp SIGSEGV under Electron-as-Node (#16127) break core IDE functionality on Linux.
  5. Memory/performance footprint of the shell safety layer — ~1.6 GiB transient WASM allocation (#15165) and ~166 MiB per-sandbox overhead in Managed Runtime workers (#16147, closed) show the safety tooling carries real cost.
  6. Security defaults diverging from documentation — Web Shell channels opening to anyone (#16144) while docs claim group access is off by default; security-sensitive reviewers are actively auditing permission paths (see also closed #13106 on cd redirect targets bypassing Write deny checks).

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw 生态日报 2026-11-03

Issues: 391 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-11-03 10:36 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-11-03

1. 今日概览

OpenClaw 在过去 24 小时内保持高度活跃：391 个 issue 有更新（222 个 open/活跃，169 个 closed），500 个 PR 有变动（306 个 open，194 个 merged/closed），并发布了一个新版本（v2026.10.10）。整体走向明显偏向功能开发——今日关闭的 issue 中很大一部分是被清扫的 stale 项，而非新近修复，这掩盖了真实的修复率。稳定性问题集中在一个主题上：会话回收中的崩溃循环/状态丢失故障、原生关闭卡死，以及 doctor 挂起，其中若干被标记为 P0/P1 和发布阻断项。安全与隐私信号同样值得关注（浏览器 CDP 结果中的凭据泄露、transcript 脱敏污染、tools.fs.workspaceOnly 绕过）。整体项目健康度：吞吐量高，但 P0/P1 积压深度偏高，且关闭速度依赖 stale 清扫。

2. 发布 — v2026.10.10

亮点

  • 备份安全：经 secret 脱敏的 Git 备份现在覆盖 PostgreSQL 导出，并省略 bundled-plugin 凭据、webhook token 及 credential blob，同时保留非机密插件状态。（#174698、#186953）——感谢 @RomneyDa、@art22s、@jlapenna。
  • Codex：changelog 被截断；所提供数据中未列出进一步变更。

破坏性变更 / 迁移说明： 所提供摘录中未明确记录。但请注意今日 issue/PR 数据中相邻的升级风险信号：

  • PR #191825（open）报告从 2026.10.10 执行 openclaw update 时，在旧版 exec-approvals.json 迁移过程中卡在 "database is locked"。这是本版本的升级路径风险，本身不算破坏性变更，但对采用者相关。
  • Issue #187917（P2）：2026.10.8 上的更新失败 updater-runtime-retention（linux/arm64，Node 26）。
  • Issue #169423（closed，stale）：codex 插件迁移在 10.1 之后卡在 unfinished。

采用建议： 升级到 2026.10.10 以获取备份安全收益是合理的，但请配合执行一次 openclaw doctor 健全性检查，并在非生产 profile 上验证 exec-approvals 迁移。另见 §5 中的 P1 doctor 挂起报告。

3. 项目进展

今日 merged/closed 的 PR（194 个 merged/closed；所提供样本中的代表性条目）：

  • PR #191813 [CLOSED] — fix(backup)：在禁用 fs-safe 原生模块的情况下修复 macOS Git 备份清理测试失败（P3）。解除本地 pnpm release:push 门禁阻塞。
  • PR #191816 [CLOSED] — perf(ci)：降低 web-fetch provider 边界检查的内存保留（P2，证据充分）。
  • PR #191826 [CLOSED] — docs(testing)：将 mock 注解与基线更新保持在一起（XS）。

已关闭 issue（今日 169 个；样本显示大量 stale 清扫）：

  • #159356 [CLOSED，stale] — llama.cpp manager/embedding HTTP 500；报告了运维层面的解决（RAM 4 GB → 8 GB）。
  • #158966 [CLOSED，stale] — 浏览器凭据化 CDP WebSocket URL 进入了面向模型的标签页结果（安全相关，但似乎是通过 stale 关闭的——请核实修复情况）。
  • #169154 [CLOSED] — 包含 Authorization: Bearer <token> 的频道消息在 transcript 幂等性冲突上失败。
  • #161208 [CLOSED，stale] — 心跳未复用 Anthropic prompt 缓存（成本影响，约 $0.40–0.95/心跳）。
  • #156864 [CLOSED，stale] — tools.alsoAllow: ["browser"] 未授予 browser 工具。

推进中的功能（证据充分、等待维护者查看的 open PR）：

  • #191715 fix(oc-path)：完成多行 frontmatter 解析（diamond lobster）。
  • #191791 fix(knowledge)：编码哈希的 Markdown 文件名。
  • #181835 fix(ui)：在 Control UI 频道会话中展示 bounded-context 警告。
  • #191749 improve(runtime)：减少 agent 准备/状态读取中的等待。

已合并功能说明： 样本中的"merged/closed PR"集合以 XS/S 级 docs、perf 和测试卫生为主——这与一个由 changelog 驱动的大型发布（v2026.10.10）已经切割、后续加固工作刚刚开始的情况一致。

4. 社区热点话题

Issue（按评论数）：

  1. #159356 — 30 条评论，CLOSED（stale）— llama.cpp manager/embedding 就绪状态不匹配（HTTP 500 Failed to read connection）。需求： 为受管子进程提供可靠的就绪/存活信号；内存压力关联。
  2. #177656 — 25 条评论，OPEN，P1 — 原生 host exec 返回 Direct shared-state reader requires current integrity admission 且无子进程结果，在稳定版 2026.10.5 上出现 28+ 次失败。需求： 向调用方暴露确定性的错误；不发生静默的共享状态损坏。
  3. #120385 — 24 条评论，OPEN，P2 — Code Mode 工具目录在 cron/memory-flush 轮次中不完整 → Unknown tool id，仅以"Exec failed."形式暴露。需求： 为非交互轮次提供完整工具目录；可操作的错误展示。
  4. #166634 — 23 条评论，OPEN，P0，发布阻断项 — 延迟回收检查点失败导致崩溃恢复后 agent 不可用（SQLite session reclamation commit checkpoint expired）。需求： gateway 死亡后的持久恢复。
  5. #178359 — 23 条评论，OPEN，P1 — doctor --fix --non-interactive 空转 15+ 分钟且无输出（macOS）。需求： 长时修复路径中的进度/可观测性。

PR（信号最强的 open 项）：

  • #163765 — iOS 个人 Tailscale 身份；XL，高合并风险（安全边界、兼容性）。状态：需要证据。
  • #191749 — 减少 runtime 等待；XL，已可交由维护者查看。
  • #186888 — 长时命令自动化的实时输出；需要安全审查。
  • #163267 — 同频道线程召回，而无需 agent 全局可见性；兼容性风险，等待作者。

深层分析： 评论密集的 issue 并非功能请求——它们是可诊断性问题。用户反复报告"静默成功"（health 显示绿色但 agent 卡死）和"不透明失败"（泛化的 Exec failed、无输出挂起）。这表明维护者下一个高价值投入应是不变式检查 + 暴露错误码，而非净新增能力。

5. 缺陷与稳定性（按严重程度排序）

P0 / 发布阻断：

Issue 状态 描述
#166634 OPEN，P0，阻断项 延迟回收提交检查点失败 → 崩溃恢复后 agent 永久 UNAVAILABLE。未发现修复 PR。
#169844 OPEN，P0，阻断项 Windows 上 Control UI Gateway 更新卡在"Activating"；计划任务被留置为 Disabled，gateway 停止。
#142821 OPEN，P0，安全审查 默认开启的 transcript 脱敏污染重放的上下文（掩码传播到命令/文件/回复中）。已关联 open PR。
#164800 OPEN，P0，修复形态清晰 2026.9.7→2026.9.8 受管更新后激活驱动死亡，需重启主机方可恢复。

P1：

  • #177656 — 共享状态 integrity-admission 错误，无子进程结果（稳定版 2026.10.5）。
  • #178359 — doctor --fix --non-interactive 空转 15+ 分钟。
  • #187900 — doctor 在启动时无限挂起，所有模式（Linux，2026.10.8）。与 #178359 为伴生问题——很可能同根。
  • #144336 — SIGUSR1 延迟重启导致关闭失败（service child cleanup identity lost）——与 #177656 同族。
  • #186684 — claude-cli 工具列表变更使原生会话失效；历史重新播种被拒 → agent 无历史重启。
  • #145309 — claude-cli 忽略 CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR；transcript 缺失导致重置。
  • #169844 — （同上）

P2 / 值得注意的回归：

  • #182891 — prompt 缓存从未复用（cache read dropped N -> 0）；成本影响。
  • #154104 — 空闲 Gateway 挂 4 个 Matrix E2EE 账户：约 50% CPU，约 52 MB/min 写入（相对 2026.7.1 的回归）。
  • #138561 — 活跃记忆召回在 2026.8.2 之后停止，info 级别下静默。
  • #173058 — 安全：通过将 state root 作为允许 cwd 绕过 tools.fs.workspaceOnly。
  • #162585 — Windows 插件源码捕获 staging 永不收敛（290 MB → 612 MB+/24 分钟）。
  • #137613 — CLI 后端上 pre-compaction 记忆刷新被禁用；明显修复会触发 compactionCount 陷阱。

修复 PR 状态： 仅 #142821 有已关联的 open PR；#164800 被标记为 fix-shape-clear。#166634、#169844、#177656、#178359、#187900 似乎尚无上游修复 PR——这一簇是该​​项目最紧迫的稳定性债务。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

高信号请求（有关联/open PR，即可能的下个版本候选）：

  • #155633 — 将 Databricks Unity Gateway 作为官方 provider。PR #155634 已 open，证据充分 → 近期可能落地。
  • #128090 — Review 文件中的渲染 Markdown 预览（👍4）。
  • #138279 — Linux aarch64 伴生构建（deb + AppImage）；Windows ARM 已发布 → 打包对称性请求。
  • #186888 — 运行中命令自动化的实时输出（PR open，安全审查）。
  • #163267 — 有作用域的同频道线程召回。

路线图形态的请求（尚无 PR，标记为产品决策）：

  • #112372 — 为 sessions_send 提供可选的 wakeOnReply（已推迟，origin-bound 完成）。
  • #138990 — 为长时前台 WebChat 运行提供可强制执行的检查点/有界让出。
  • #158068 — Swarm 群体的自适应测试时计算。
  • #107433 — openclaw backup 的 manifest 支撑的刻意省略（platinum hermit，安全审查）。
  • #158800 — 在 Control UI 中 /new 之后浏览/分叉先前的频道片段。
  • #136271 — 用于频道文件上传的 msteams 动态 SharePoint 站点解析。

预测： 下一个补丁版本可能落地 Databricks provider（#155634）、实时自动化输出（#186888），以及 oc-path/knowledge 文件名修复（#191715、#191791）。语言/locale 修复（#191806、#191823）表明一轮本地化工作正在进行中。

7. 用户反馈摘要

痛点（反复出现、跨 issue）：

  1. 虚假绿色 health / 静默卡死。 #159789（agent 锁定时"health 保持绿色"）、#166634（永久 UNAVAILABLE）、#177656（无子进程结果）、#120385（仅"Exec failed"）。用户若不翻日志就无法区分健康与卡死。
  2. Doctor 是负担。 #178359 和 #187900 均报告 doctor 在多个 OS 上挂起且无输出——本应作为恢复工具的工具自身不可靠，加剧了故障。
  3. 升级脆弱性。 #169844、#164800、#187917、#183479、#169423、#157812：Windows 计划任务挂起、激活驱动死亡、保留包阻塞、codex 迁移停滞。多跳升级（#169423）是真实的运维隐患。
  4. 成本与性能回归。 #182891 和 #161208（prompt 缓存不复用）、#154104（Matrix E2EE 空闲消耗约 50% CPU / 52 MB/min）——给运维者带来可衡量的基础设施成本。
  5. 安全面。 #158966（CDP 凭据流向模型）、#173058（workspaceOnly 绕过）、#142821（脱敏污染）——信任边界卫生是现实关切。

数据中可见的使用场景： 具有重度频道路由的多 agent 集群（Telegram/WeChat/Matrix/Slack）、长生命周期会话（#151962 中约 310k token）、由 Claude 订阅驱动的 CLI（#145309、#186684、#158922）、Windows 桌面/计划任务部署（#169844、#162585），以及气隙/LAN 本地模型服务器（llama.cpp、Ollama、llmman——见 #175923、#175414、#174877、#174861）。

满意信号： 在 provider 广度上有强劲的社区贡献（#155634）、有针对性的 UI/docs 打磨 PR（许多由 @ericcurtin、@vincentkoc 提交），以及被列为亮点的 2026.10.10 备份安全工作。不满意集中在运维可靠性与诊断不透明上——同样这些主题主导了评论数前 10 的榜单。

8. 积压关注（需维护者注意）

条目 存在时长 为何重要
#142821（P0，安全，已关联 PR） 约 2 个月 P0 安全/数据丢失且有一个 open PR——尽管 P0 标签仍存在 stale-PR 风险。
#112313（死信出站队列，永久性） 约 3.5 个月 Diamond-lobster 评级；条目不可读/不可删除；health 永远计入它们。无修复。
#107433（备份省略，platinum，安全审查） 约 4 个月 阻塞安全的备份/恢复工作流；产品 + 安全决策待定。
#137613（CLI 后端记忆刷新禁用） 约 2 个月 Diamond-lobster，标记为产品决策；已知陷阱有文档但无负责人。
#144797（复用的 claude-cli 会话保留已删除的 --mcp-config，工具 401） 约 2 个月 陈旧但可复现；影响 auth-provider。
#112372（推迟的 wakeOnReply） 约 3.5 个月 陈旧，产品决策；是异步编排需求的基础。
#90074（OpenAI 图像生成忽略 Codex OAuth） 约 5 个月 非常旧的 diamond-lobster；1 👍。
#163765（iOS 个人身份，XL）— 1 个月 长生命周期的 XL PR，带安全边界合并风险，"需要证据"。
#155634（Databricks provider）— 6 周 证据充分的功能 PR，等待维护者查看。

元观察： 若干安全相关 issue（#158966、#161208）被作为 stale 关闭，而非修复——建议进行策略审查，确保 stale 清扫不会静默地让未解决的信任边界发现被搁置。

数据窗口：2026-11-02 → 2026-11-03 UTC。评论数反映样本前 50 的 issue / 前 30 的 PR。PR 信息流中的 Comments: undefined 是数据字段缺失，而非零活动。

横向生态对比

跨项目对比报告 — AI Agent / 个人 AI 助手开源生态

数据窗口：2026-11-02 → 2026-11-03 UTC | 项目：OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、IronClaw、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw

1. 生态概览

本次调研的五个项目处于同一收敛品类下的不同成熟阶段：持久化、多渠道、具备工具执行、记忆与网关编排能力的 AI Agent。活跃度呈现明显两极分化——OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、QwenPaw 与 ZeroClaw 均处于迁移后或发布前加固阶段（统一网关回归、v0.9.0 门禁、2.3.0 beta 稳定化），而 IronClaw 实际上处于休眠状态，仅有自动化依赖变更。整个生态的主导工程成本已不再是模型能力，而是运行可靠性：会话持久性、静默失败诊断与安全边界执行。社区成员的安全审计如今在至少三个项目中已成为常规的、逐行引用的活动，表明该生态正被作为真实基础设施而非玩具助手部署。贡献量与维护者审查/合并能力之间始终存在缺口。

2. 活跃度对比

项目 Issue（触及 / 开启 / 关闭） PR（触及 / 开启 / 合并-关闭） 发布状态 健康评分（分析师） 备注
OpenClaw 391 / 222 / 169 500 / 306 / 194 已发布 v2026.10.10（备份安全） 6.5 / 10 — 吞吐量高，P0/P1 积压深 关闭速度因陈旧清理而虚高；4 个未关闭 P0 阻塞项，其中若干无修复 PR
Hermes Agent 50 / ~48 / 12+ 50 / 38 / 12 v0.22.6 汇总（约 776 个 PR），变更日志推迟至 v0.23.0 7.0 / 10 — 承压但可运转 统一网关（#106742）余波占主导；47 条评论的分诊帖
IronClaw 0 / 0 / 0 4 / 2 / 2 无 5.0 / 10 — 稳定但休眠 仅 dependabot 的 rustls 升级；窗口内无人工创作活动
QwenPaw 18 / ~12 / 6 37 / ~26 / 11 无（2.3.0-beta.1–b3 测试中） 7.5 / 10 — Issue→PR 转化强 当日快速修复；一个未处理的安全问题（#8513）
ZeroClaw 50 / 48 / 2 50 / 40 / 10 无（v0.9.0 门禁进行中） 6.0 / 10 — 贡献高，审查瓶颈 开启:关闭比 24:1；S1 发布门禁缺陷仍开启

健康评分为吞吐量、积压深度、关键缺陷的修复 PR 覆盖率与发布节奏的定性综合——非项目背书的指标。

解读： OpenClaw 与 ZeroClaw 存在相同的结构性问题——缺陷发现速度超过修复吞吐量与审查能力。QwenPaw 相对接单量拥有最佳的关闭纪律。Hermes Agent 拥有最高的绝对 PR 量，但正在消化一次大型架构迁移。IronClaw 的零人工活动窗口是这组中唯一的真正红旗。

3. OpenClaw 的定位

相对同行的优势

  • 最大的绝对社区与吞吐量——24 小时内触及 391 个 Issue / 500 个 PR，按窗口计约为 Hermes 或 ZeroClaw 的 8–10 倍，比 QwenPaw 高出数个数量级。
  • 最成熟的发布纪律——本窗口内唯一一个附带已记录安全加固内容的版本化发布（覆盖 PostgreSQL 与插件凭据的脱敏 Git 备份）。
  • 最广的提供商与渠道覆盖——Databricks provider PR 附带充分证明（#155634），另有 Telegram/WeChat/Matrix/Slack 路由已投入生产使用。
  • Issue 层面明确的安全文化——P0 安全标签（transcript redaction poisoning #142821、tools.fs.workspaceOnly 绕过 #173058）以严重性标签跟踪，而非被埋没。

看似强大实则薄弱之处

  • 陈旧清理式关闭模式是真实风险：两个安全相关 Issue（#158966 CDP 凭据泄露、#161208 prompt-cache 成本）被以陈旧为由关闭，而非修复。这是同行（尤其是 ZeroClaw 逐行引用的审计文化）处理得更好的治理欠账。
  • P0 阻塞项缺乏修复 PR（#166634 崩溃恢复后永久 UNAVAILABLE、#169844 Windows 激活挂起）——贡献者的广度并未转化为对最难项的归属。

技术路线差异

  • OpenClaw 依托丰富的插件/扩展模型，捆绑凭据并具备原生宿主执行路径（Direct shared-state reader、完整性准入错误）——比 QwenPaw 的 Python/AgentScope 栈或 Hermes 的网关中心设计更重。
  • 它是本组中唯一将专用备份/恢复子系统附带安全审查作为一等发布特性的项目——表明其有贴近企业的意图。

社区规模对比： OpenClaw ≫ Hermes ≈ ZeroClaw > QwenPaw ≫ IronClaw。贡献者 handle 的长尾（许多为顺手的文档/UI PR）表明 OpenClaw 已跨入广泛贡献者领域，而 Hermes 与 ZeroClaw 仍呈现集中、重复贡献者的模式。

4. 共同技术焦点领域

以下需求在三个或更多项目中反复出现，使其成为生态级而非项目特定的问题：

需求 项目 具体需求
消除静默失败 / 可诊断性 OpenClaw（#166634、#177656、#120385）、Hermes（#143547）、QwenPaw（#8488、#8505、#8549）、ZeroClaw（#12014、#12194、#12203） 在启动/配置时大声失败；呈现可操作的错误码而非 "Exec failed" 或 "unknown"；健康检查必须检测卡死状态，而非仅存活。
跨传输的会话/轮次持久性 OpenClaw（#166634 崩溃恢复）、Hermes（#146344 admission_conflict、#145889 网关卡死）、ZeroClaw（#7759 轮次/WS 解耦）、QwenPaw（#8532 仅追加会话存储） 长时间运行的轮次必须经受重载、断连、重启；仅追加/带检查点的会话状态正成为收敛设计。
对已声明配置的安全边界执行 OpenClaw（#173058 workspaceOnly 绕过）、ZeroClaw（#9394 pairing_dashboard 未读取、#12052 XFF 伪造）、QwenPaw（#8513 无门禁 shell 操作）、Hermes（#135415 凭据回退） 被接受但未读取的配置键；默认开启却污染上下文的保护；已记录却不运行的守卫。主题是**"宣称 ≠ 执行"。**
上下文窗口 / 提供商配置正确性 ZeroClaw（#12014/#12194 静默 32k 回退）、QwenPaw（#8496 max_tokens 注入、#8236 Ollama num_ctx）、OpenClaw（#182891 prompt-cache 未复用）、Hermes（#148380 Anthropic json_mode） BYO-provider 用户遭遇静默错误；需要验证配置并对未知模型大声失败。
插件/依赖生命周期健壮性 OpenClaw（捆绑插件备份）、Hermes（#148337 catalog 固定）、QwenPaw（#8265 热安装、#8553 DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED、#8554 插件 CLI）、ZeroClaw（#11703 tool_search 缓存失效） 共享依赖模型导致级联激活失败；插件加载必须隔离且发行版无关。
Windows 平台对等性 Hermes（#68128、#144964）、QwenPaw（今日 6+ 个 Windows 缺陷）、OpenClaw（#162585、#169844）、ZeroClaw（#12126/#12127 UNC 凭据泄露） CRLF、编码（GBK/CP932）、PyInstaller 资源、UNC 路径、计划任务——尽管有真实用户基础，Windows 始终是二等公民。

跨领域根因： 大多数"不稳定"报告实际上是可观测性失败——系统正在做某事（降级回退、静默跳过、陈旧配置），而用户无法将其与挂起或缺陷区分。

5. 差异化分析

维度 OpenClaw Hermes Agent IronClaw QwenPaw ZeroClaw
功能焦点 全栈助手：提供商、渠道、备份、宿主执行 桌面 + 机器人编排 + 插件 catalog 基准测试/延迟工具 插件生态 + 长会话存储 + 渠道 安全优先守护进程：配对、OIDC、A2A、网关可靠性

标志性弱点 陈旧清理掩盖未解决的安全问题 迁移余波；永久卡死缺陷（#145889） 无活动 安全问题 #8513 未分配；Windows 缺陷 24:1 开启:关闭；审查能力

架构分歧说明： Hermes 与 ZeroClaw 近期都集中到基于网关的会话准入模型——两者现在都在支付回归代价（准入冲突、profile 作用域渗漏、worker 权限拒绝）。OpenClaw 使用共享状态 + 完整性准入模型，失效类别不同（检查点过期、身份丢失）。QwenPaw 正收敛于仅追加会话存储，若顺利落地，可能被证明是三种设计中最健壮的——值得作为参考实现关注。

6. 社区动能与成熟度

第一梯队——高动能、广泛贡献者： OpenClaw。 绝对活跃度最大；生产级贡献者多样性；但动能部分人为（陈旧清理），P0 归属薄弱。功能面成熟度高，可靠性中等。

第二梯队——高动能、迁移承压： Hermes Agent 与 ZeroClaw。

  • Hermes 展现强劲的维护者吞吐量与高度参与的社区作为 QA 层运作（47 条评论分诊）。它正处于架构迁移后的稳定化——v0.23.0 将是稳定化发布。
  • ZeroClaw 正快速迭代迈向安全+可靠性 v0.9.0，但受限于审查能力。其社区是本组中安全素养最高的。

第二梯队 b——高动能、纪律性关闭： QwenPaw。 绝对量低于第一/二梯队，但拥有最佳的 Issue 到 PR 转化与最干净的关闭比。处于活跃 beta 稳定化——大多数"缺陷"是 beta 测试面，而非架构腐化。本组中从报告到修复最快的路径。

第三梯队——休眠： IronClaw。 零人工创作活动；仅自动化依赖升级。安全上稳定低风险，但本窗口无法评估为活跃维护——在依赖它之前监控人工 PR 的回归。

成熟度框定： 功能成熟但可靠性不成熟（OpenClaw、Hermes、ZeroClaw）是常见模式；QwenPaw 最接近均衡；IronClaw 仅维护。本组中无项目达到"可靠性成熟"。

7. 趋势信号（面向 AI Agent 开发者）

提取自跨项目社区反馈，按信号强度排序：

  1. 可靠性是新差异化因素——诊断不透明是首要抱怨。 在所有四个活跃项目中，参与度最高的帖子是可诊断性问题，而非功能请求。可操作项： 在添加能力之前，投资于不变量检查 + 呈现错误码 + 进度可观测性（尤其在长时间运行的修复/doctor 路径中）。"虚假绿色健康"是信任杀手。

  2. 会话/轮次持久性是架构战场。 多个项目独立收敛于仅追加、带检查点、传输解耦的会话状态（ZeroClaw #7759、QwenPaw #8532、OpenClaw 崩溃恢复 #166634）。可操作项： 从第一天起就为经受重载/重启/断连的轮次设计；将 WS/socket 生命周期视为短暂。

  3. "宣称 ≠ 执行"是主导的安全失效模式。 配置键被接受但未读取（ZeroClaw）、默认开启的保护污染数据（OpenClaw）、已声明的守卫未起门禁作用（QwenPaw）。可操作项： 在启动时验证并执行配置，对未知/未读取键大声失败，并审计安全开关确实运行。 社区安全审计（逐行引用、可复现）如今已是预期——为其构建。

  4. BYO-provider 正确性是一类静默数据丢失。 未知模型与缺失上下文窗口配置静默回退到错误默认值（ZeroClaw 32k、QwenPaw max_tokens 注入、OpenClaw 缓存未复用）。可操作项： 对模型/提供商配置进行大声验证与明确的上下文窗口契约；不要假设。

  5. 成本可观测性是一等用户需求。 Prompt-cache 未复用、空闲 CPU/GPU 消耗（Hermes 桌面 25–45%、OpenClaw Matrix E2EE 约 50% CPU）、心跳缓存未命中——用户测量并反感基础设施成本。可操作项： 呈现缓存命中率、空闲资源使用与每轮成本；将缓存稳定性视为特性（例如延迟 MCP 加载导致缓存失效，ZeroClaw #11703）。

  6. 插件/依赖隔离是生态健康的前提。 共享依赖模型导致级联激活失败；catalog 固定与插件 CLI/扩展点正浮现。可操作项： 隔离插件依赖环境、固定 catalog 条目、暴露资源生命周期钩子——插件生态是护城河，那里的脆弱会阻碍第三方增长。

  7. Windows 与 i18n 是真实、服务不足的细分市场。 一致的 Windows 特定缺陷簇与明确的非英语部署需求（Hermes 17 语言对等、QwenPaw 中文 Windows 数据丢失修复）。可操作项： 将 Windows 与本地化作为一等测试目标，而非事后考虑——编码（GBK/CP932/CRLF）、路径处理（UNC、中文路径）与打包完整性。

  8. 维护者审查能力，而非贡献量，是生态瓶颈。 OpenClaw 无归属的 P0、ZeroClaw 停滞的 S1 修复 PR、QwenPaw 相互竞争的重复 CRLF PR 都指向同一方向。对开发者的可操作项： 提交可复现、逐行引用的报告（获得快速处理的都具备此特征）；对维护者：对安全标签 Issue 设定明确分诊 SLA并合并重复修复努力。

决策者要点： OpenClaw 在功能面上最广、最接近生产就绪，但背负未解决的可靠性与陈旧清理式安全欠账——采用时需以 doctor 优先的升级纪律并对"以陈旧关闭"的安全项进行独立验证。Hermes 与 ZeroClaw 正稳定化迈向可靠性发布，是优先考虑安全严谨与持久会话的团队的最佳选择，前提是能容忍迁移期摩擦。QwenPaw 为渠道/插件密集与中文 Windows 部署提供最佳关闭纪律与最快修复周期。IronClaw 在人工创作活动恢复前应视为休眠。贯穿所有项目：将可观测性与会话持久性作为核心工程预算，而非打磨项。

  • iOS beta 链接失效： 官方 TestFlight 邀请返回"Beta Not Found"（#147556，👍2）——入门障碍。

使用场景（满意信号）：

  • 非开发者文档工作流： 桌面端用于生成客户就绪的 PDF/DOCX/HTML（#148435）——超越开发者的健康扩展。
  • 多 bot 协作： 用户跨机器构建群聊（#148418/#148422）——Bot Mode 正被用于真实编排。
  • i18n 需求 来自非英文部署（#141738、#148341）——国际用户群真实且积极发声。
  • 积极信号： 47 条评论的众包分诊（#143547）显示了一个积极参与、愿意共同调试的社区——尽管有摩擦，这是强有力的留存指标。

#8234 read/edit/grep 中的 GBK/CP936 解码 创建于 2026-10-14，审查中 中文 Windows 的数据丢失修复；已停滞 20 天。PR
#8236 Ollama num_ctx 上下文大小 创建于 2026-10-14，审查中 本地模型准确性；已停滞 20 天。PR
#4312 agent.json 热重载范围（MCP、Skills） 创建于 2026-05-14，今日关闭，历经 6 个月 关闭良好，但表明积压深度——功能请求可能搁置数月。Issue
#8013 技能池下载超时（12,994 个文件，80MB） 创建于 2026-09-29，今日关闭 大型技能处理需要三层修复（前端 30 秒中止、后端复制、最终工作区落地）。Issue

建议： 维护者应 (1) 立即将 #8513 分配给具备安全能力的贡献者，(2) 选择一个 CRLF 修复（#8235 或 #8433）并关闭另一个并给予致谢，(3) 批量审查来自贡献者 Li-john1021 的三个停滞的 2026-10-14 PR（#8234、#8235、#8236）以保持参与度。

摘要基于 2026-11-03 的 GitHub 活动数据生成。所有链接指向 github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw。

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-11-03

1. 今日概览

ZeroClaw 今日开发活跃度极高：过去 24 小时更新了 50 个 issue（48 个开启/活跃，仅 2 个关闭）和 50 个 PR（40 个开启，10 个已合并/关闭），无新版本发布。项目显然处于 v0.9.0 前的加固阶段——多个 P1 标记项引用了 release:v0.9.0（配对强制、发布体积门控、Docker 源码构建），安全/身份访问相关工作主导了新缺陷流入。Issue 队列并未缩减——今日约 24:1 的开启/关闭比表明，相对于缺陷发现速度，分诊与修复吞吐量正成为日益增长的瓶颈。维护者注意力明显分散于网关安全（配对、OIDC、X-Forwarded-For 信任）、agent 回合生命周期以及 provider 上下文窗口正确性。整体项目健康度在贡献量上表现强劲，但在 issue 关闭和发布门控验证方面显现压力。

2. 版本发布

过去 24 小时无新版本发布。（issue 报告中已知的最新发布版本为 zeroclaw v0.8.7 / web v0.8.x；v0.9.0 工作正在进行中。）

3. 项目进展

今日合并/关闭的 PR（共 10 个），值得注意的项目：

  • PR #12208 — fix(web): restore an in-flight turn after a reload：持久化乐观提示词 + 部分答案/推理的节流 localStorage 快照，使聊天重新加载后不再丢失工作。直接补充网关 WS 生命周期 issue #7759。
  • PR #12209 — fix(web): require confirmation and neutral wording for stopped turns：阻止意外的双击取消，并移除 [interrupted by user] 持久化噪音。
  • PR #11054 — WhatsApp Web：主题分隔线（---、***、___）和 setext 标题现在正确渲染，不再作为字面标点泄漏（关闭 #11052）。
  • PR #11739 — Telegram：回复完成时现在会撤回确认反应（修复了缺失的 remove_reaction 覆盖）。
  • PR #11270 — CI：zeroclaw-desktop 测试现已在 macOS、Linux 和 Windows 上运行，填补了其他所有 workspace 任务均排除 desktop crate 的覆盖缺口。
  • PR #12202 — 依赖升级（rust-all 组，35 项更新），同日被 #12215 取代。

进行中的高价值工作： PR #11921（仅追加会话事件历史——架构性，XL）、#11965（可选加入的 OIDC 仪表盘登录）、#12213（强制执行 [gateway.pairing_dashboard]，修复 #9394）、#11712（提取 zeroclaw-a2a crate）、#11456（子进程内存看门狗）。

4. 社区热点

项目 活跃度 潜在需求
#7759 — 将网关 WebSocket 生命周期与 agent 回合生命周期解耦 8 条评论，P1，进行中，风险:高 用户希望后台回合能在断连后存活——在不稳定/移动连接上长时间运行的 agent 工作的可靠性。
#10926 — Matrix send_via 将 peer 用户身份视为房间目标 7 条评论，P2 跨通道寻址语义令人困惑；A2A/peer 消息传递需要精确的目标解析。
#12014 — 自定义 OpenAI 兼容 provider 静默假定 32k 上下文 5 条评论，S1 自带 provider 的用户遭遇有效回合被本地静默拒绝；需要明确、响亮的配置错误。
#9394 — pairing_dashboard 被接受但未被读取；配对码永不过期 5 条评论，P1，v0.9.0 安全期望：文档化的配置必须实际被强制执行；修复 PR #12213 已开启。
#11703 — tool_search 激活破坏提示词缓存 4 条评论 对成本敏感且使用延迟 MCP 加载的用户；希望系统提示词稳定。

模式： 热门讨论串由长时间运行回合的可靠性、自带模型配置正确性以及宣称但未强制执行的安全配置主导。

5. 缺陷与稳定性

按严重程度排序；除注明外，均为今日新报告/刷新：

S1 — 工作流受阻

  • #12210 — 今日新增。 每个源码 Docker 镜像构建（Dockerfile、.debian、.alpine）在依赖预取阶段失败，因为未复制 tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer。发布门控风险（P1，v0.9.0）；尚无修复 PR。
  • #12187 — 通道缓存回合归一化将用户回合合并进 role=tool 信封，在严格 provider 上永久污染对话。未识别到修复 PR。
  • #12014 — 32k 上下文窗口回退拒绝有效回合（见社区热点）。
  • #9859 — Distroless 发布镜像缺少 sh，破坏 runtime.shell webhook（S1，自 8 月起持续）。
  • #12126 — Windows UNC 附件路径可使守护进程向攻击者控制的 SMB/WebDAV 服务器认证（凭据泄露）。

P1 / 高风险

  • #12194 — 今日新增。 未知模型静默回退到 UNCONFIGURED_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FALLBACK = 32_000；与 #12014 同属根因家族——修复可能应合并处理。
  • #12203 — web_search_tool 在无 tools-external 时被静默编译排除；未发出警告（#11221 的回归）。
  • #9394 — 配对码永不过期（修复 PR #12213 已开启 ✅）。

安全（身份/访问，S2 类）

  • #12052 — 限流器信任第一个 X-Forwarded-For 条目 → 在追加式代理后可伪造回环豁免。
  • #12050 — OIDC 回调令牌页面无浏览器绑定 → 登录 CSRF。
  • #12053 — /api/docs 在仪表盘源上加载未固定版本的第三方脚本（无 SRI）。
  • #12127 — git_operations 在 Windows 上于授权前触碰 gitdir:/commondir/alternates 路径（UNC 凭据泄露向量）。

S2/S3 降级行为

  • #10926（Matrix）、#10924（运行时命令回复进入语音路由）、#12167（send_message_to_peer 忽略自主级别/操作预算——策略绕过）、#12104（OpenAI Responses 丢弃工具结果图像）、#12133（Windows 环境允许列表遗漏 APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA）。
  • #9562（WebChat 自动滚动）、#12186（zerocode --agent 被解析但未使用）、#12087（工具开关双重保存）——S3 UX 问题。

评估： 安全集群（#12050/#12052/#12053/#12126/#12127）似乎出自同一报告者的单次审计系列，值得在 v0.9.0 前给出统一的安全发布响应。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

  • #7759 — 后台/可恢复网关回合（P1，进行中，web 侧支持已在 #12208/#12209 中合并）。极有可能进入 v0.9.0。
  • #10893 — 通道消息的生成中途转向（状态:blocked；管道存在但无生产者）。#7759 的自然搭档。
  • #12183 — 活跃 agent 的运行时提示词/命令拦截与注入——同一"飞行中可控性"主题。
  • #12181 — Web 托管文档上传（#9488 第二阶段 Web 切片），默认关闭——可能是 OIDC 后的下一个小版本。
  • #12191 — Qdrant 内存后端的混合密集+BM25 召回（与 SQLite 后端对齐）——一个合理的中期路线图项。
  • #12107 — socket 重开时显示分离回合的答案——#11965 的后续，与 #7759 配对。

对 v0.9.0 的预测： 强制配对仪表盘（#12213）、OIDC 仪表盘登录（#11965）、网关回合解耦（#7759）以及发布/CI 修复（#12210、#11580、#11272）——即 v0.9.0 看起来是一个安全 + 可靠性版本，而非功能扩展版本。

7. 用户反馈摘要

  • 配置信任是最响亮的抱怨。 用户报告配置键"被接受但完全未被读取"（#9394）以及默认值静默假定错误值（#12014、#12194、#12203）——反复出现的关键词是静默地。未满足的期望：无效或降级的配置应在启动时响亮失败，而非在回合中途。
  • 长时间运行的工作必须能在传输层存活。 多个讨论串（#7759、#9562、#12107、#12208、#12209）追溯到用户将 web 聊天视为生产控制台，并被重新加载、断连或自动滚动抢走滚动位置所困扰——这是移动/不稳定网络上真实日常使用的明确迹象。
  • 高级用户正在运行多 agent/多通道拓扑。 Matrix peer 路由（#10926）、send_message_to_peer 自主绕过（#12167）以及回合中途转向（#10893）来自运营 agent 组的用户，而非单一助手。
  • 安全报告者正在进行仔细、逐行引用的审计（#9394、#12050、#12052、#12126、#12127）——社区将 ZeroClaw 视为具有真实威胁模型（代理、OIDC、Windows UNC）的可部署守护进程，这是成熟的标志，但也表明积累了安全债务。
  • 满意度信号： web/聊天 UX 修复的快速周转（同日 PR #12208/#12209）表明维护者对用户最常提出的前端痛点反应迅速。

8. 积压关注

因年龄、严重程度或阻塞状态而需要维护者关注的项：

  • #9859 — Distroless 镜像缺少 sh（S1，自 2026-08-09 开启，仅 2 条评论，1 个 👍）。长期存在的发布产物阻塞项，无关联修复。
  • #11580 — x86_64 Linux 二进制约 0.7 MB，低于 64 MiB 上限；需要记录余量策略决策（needs-maintainer-review，v0.9.0）。这是门控决策，而非编码任务——适合本周维护者电话会议。
  • #10893 — 转向管道存在但无生产者；状态:blocked 且无归属。值得一个设计决策或明确推迟。
  • #9394 — 尽管修复 PR #12213 已开启，该 issue 自 7 月以来一直悬而未决，标记 release:v0.9.0；审查容量是瓶颈。
  • #11272 — Linux/Windows 桌面内核缺失仪表盘嵌入的发布修复，自 2026-09-30 开启且无评论；若未合并，已发布的桌面构建将明显损坏。
  • #11456 — 子进程内存看门狗，needs-maintainer-review，自 10 月 2 日开启；对不可信 shell 安全有价值但停滞。
  • #11052 — 今日关闭 ✅，仅作为解决说明列出。

底线： ZeroClaw 高度活跃，明显正收敛于一个安全与可靠性导向的 v0.9.0，但开启:关闭 issue 比（24:1）以及若干陈旧的 S1 项（#9859、#11272）表明，审查/合并容量——而非贡献量——才是项目当前的约束。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-03

Issues: 391 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-03 10:36 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-03

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remained highly active over the last 24 hours, with 391 issues updated (222 open/active, 169 closed) and 500 PRs touched (306 open, 194 merged/closed), plus a new release (v2026.10.10). The trajectory is clearly feature-development-heavy — a large share of today's issue closures are stale items being swept rather than fresh fixes, which masks the true fix rate. Stability concerns cluster around a theme: crash-loop/state-loss failures in session reclamation, native close wedging, and doctor hangs, several tagged P0/P1 and release blockers. Security and privacy signal is also notable (credential leakage in browser CDP results, transcript redaction poisoning, tools.fs.workspaceOnly bypass). Overall project health: high throughput, but elevated P0/P1 backlog depth and dependent on stale-sweeps for closure velocity.

2. Releases — v2026.10.10

Highlights

  • Backup safety: secret-redacted Git backups now cover PostgreSQL exports and omit bundled-plugin credentials, webhook tokens, and credential blobs, preserving nonsecret plugin state. (#174698, #186953) — thanks @RomneyDa, @art22s, @jlapenna.
  • Codex: changelog truncated; no further changes listed in the provided data.

Breaking changes / migration notes: None explicitly documented in the provided excerpt. However, note the adjacent upgrade-risk signals from today's issue/PR data:

  • PR #191825 (open) reports openclaw update from 2026.10.10 stalling at "database is locked" during legacy exec-approvals.json migration. This is an upgrade-path risk from this release, not a breaking change per se, but relevant to adopters.
  • Issue #187917 (P2): update failure updater-runtime-retention on 2026.10.8 (linux/arm64, Node 26).
  • Issue #169423 (closed, stale): codex plugin migration stuck unfinished after 10.1.

Adoption guidance: upgrade to 2026.10.10 is reasonable for backup-safety benefits, but pair it with a openclaw doctor sanity pass and verify exec-approvals migration on a non-production profile. See also the P1 doctor-hang reports in §5.

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs today (194 merged/closed; representative items from the provided sample):

  • PR #191813 [CLOSED] — fix(backup): macOS Git-backup cleanup test failures with fs-safe native disabled (P3). Unblocks local pnpm release:push gate.
  • PR #191816 [CLOSED] — perf(ci): reduce web-fetch provider boundary check memory retention (P2, proof sufficient).
  • PR #191826 [CLOSED] — docs(testing): keep mock annotations and baseline updates together (XS).

Closed issues (169 today; sample shows heavy stale sweep):

  • #159356 [CLOSED, stale] — llama.cpp manager/embedding HTTP 500; operational resolution reported (RAM 4 GB → 8 GB).
  • #158966 [CLOSED, stale] — browser credentialed CDP WebSocket URLs reached model-facing tab results (security-relevant, but appears closed via staleness — verify remediation).
  • #169154 [CLOSED] — channel message containing Authorization: Bearer <token> failing on transcript idempotency conflict.
  • #161208 [CLOSED, stale] — heartbeats not reusing Anthropic prompt cache (cost impact, ~$0.40–0.95/heartbeat).
  • #156864 [CLOSED, stale] — tools.alsoAllow: ["browser"] not granting the browser tool.

Features advanced (open PRs with sufficient proof, pending maintainer look):

  • #191715 fix(oc-path): complete multiline frontmatter parsing (diamond lobster).
  • #191791 fix(knowledge): encoded-hash Markdown filenames.
  • #181835 fix(ui): surface bounded-context warning in Control UI channel conversations.
  • #191749 improve(runtime): reduce waits in agent preparation/status reads.

Merged-feature note: The sample's "merged/closed PR" set is dominated by XS/S docs, perf, and test hygiene — consistent with a large changelog-driven release already cut (v2026.10.10) and follow-up hardening beginning.

4. Community Hot Topics

Issues (by comments):

  1. #159356 — 30 comments, CLOSED (stale) — llama.cpp manager/embedding readiness mismatch (HTTP 500 Failed to read connection). Need: reliable readiness/liveness signaling for managed child processes; memory-pressure correlation.
  2. #177656 — 25 comments, OPEN, P1 — Native host exec returns Direct shared-state reader requires current integrity admission with no child result, 28+ failures on stable 2026.10.5. Need: deterministic error surfaced to callers; no silent shared-state corruption.
  3. #120385 — 24 comments, OPEN, P2 — Code Mode tool catalog incomplete for cron/memory-flush turns → Unknown tool id, surfaced only as "Exec failed." Need: complete tool catalog for non-interactive turns; actionable error surfaces.
  4. #166634 — 23 comments, OPEN, P0, release blocker — Late reclamation checkpoint failure leaves agent unavailable after crash recovery (SQLite session reclamation commit checkpoint expired). Need: durable recovery after gateway death.
  5. #178359 — 23 comments, OPEN, P1 — doctor --fix --non-interactive idles 15+ min with no output (macOS). Need: progress/observability in long-running repair paths.

PRs (highest-signal open):

  • #163765 — iOS personal Tailscale identity; XL, high merge-risk (security boundary, compatibility). Status: needs proof.
  • #191749 — runtime wait reduction; XL, ready for maintainer look.
  • #186888 — live output for long-running command automations; security-review required.
  • #163267 — same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility; compatibility risk, waiting on author.

Underlying analysis: The comment-heavy issues are not feature requests — they are diagnosability problems. Users repeatedly report "silent success" (health green while agent wedged) and "opaque failures" (generic Exec failed, hangs without output). This suggests the next high-value maintainer investment is invariant checks + surfaced error codes, not net-new capabilities.

5. Bugs & Stability (ranked by severity)

P0 / release-blocking:

Issue Status Description
#166634 OPEN, P0, blocker Late reclamation commit checkpoint failure → agent permanently UNAVAILABLE after crash recovery. No fix PR identified.
#169844 OPEN, P0, blocker Control UI Gateway update on Windows hangs at "Activating"; Scheduled Task left Disabled, gateway stopped.
#142821 OPEN, P0, security-review Default-on transcript redaction poisons replayed context (masks propagate into commands/files/replies). Linked PR open.
#164800 OPEN, P0, fix-shape clear 2026.9.7→2026.9.8 managed update leaves activation driver dead until host reboot.

P1:

  • #177656 — shared-state integrity-admission error, no child result (stable 2026.10.5).
  • #178359 — doctor --fix --non-interactive idle 15+ min.
  • #187900 — doctor hangs indefinitely at startup, all modes (Linux, 2026.10.8). Companion to #178359 — likely common root.
  • #144336 — SIGUSR1 deferred restart fails shutdown (service child cleanup identity lost) — same family as #177656.
  • #186684 — claude-cli tool-list change invalidates native session; history reseed refused → agent restarts with no history.
  • #145309 — claude-cli ignores CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; missing-transcript resets.
  • #169844 — (also above)

P2 / regressions of note:

  • #182891 — prompt cache never reused (cache read dropped N -> 0); cost impact.
  • #154104 — idle Gateway with 4 Matrix E2EE accounts: ~50% CPU, ~52 MB/min writes (regression vs 2026.7.1).
  • #138561 — active-memory recall stops after 2026.8.2, silent at info level.
  • #173058 — security: tools.fs.workspaceOnly bypass via state root as allowed cwd.
  • #162585 — Windows plugin source-capture staging never converges (290 MB → 612 MB+/24 min).
  • #137613 — pre-compaction memory flush disabled on CLI backends; obvious fix hits compactionCount trap.

Fix-PR status: Only #142821 has a linked open PR; #164800 is tagged fix-shape-clear. #166634, #169844, #177656, #178359, #187900 appear to have no upstream fix PR yet — the cluster is the project's most urgent stability debt.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

High-signal requests (with linked/open PRs, i.e., likely next-release candidates):

  • #155633 — Databricks Unity Gateway as official provider. PR #155634 open, proof sufficient → plausible near-term.
  • #128090 — rendered Markdown preview in Review files (👍4).
  • #138279 — Linux aarch64 companion builds (deb + AppImage); Windows ARM already ships → packaging symmetry request.
  • #186888 — live output for running command automations (PR open, security review).
  • #163267 — scoped same-channel thread recall.

Roadmap-shaped requests (no PR yet, product-decision tagged):

  • #112372 — opt-in wakeOnReply for sessions_send (deferred, origin-bound completion).
  • #138990 — enforceable checkpoints/bounded yields for long foreground WebChat runs.
  • #158068 — adaptive test-time compute for Swarm populations.
  • #107433 — manifest-backed intentional omissions for openclaw backup (platinum hermit, security review).
  • #158800 — browse/fork prior channel segments after /new in Control UI.
  • #136271 — msteams dynamic SharePoint site resolution for channel file uploads.

Prediction: next patch release likely lands Databricks provider (#155634), live automation output (#186888), and oc-path/knowledge filename fixes (#191715, #191791). Language/locale fixes (#191806, #191823) suggest a localization pass is in flight.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (recurring, cross-issue):

  1. False-green health / silent wedging. #159789 ("health stays green" while agent locked), #166634 (permanent UNAVAILABLE), #177656 (no child result), #120385 (only "Exec failed"). Users cannot distinguish healthy from wedged without log spelunking.
  2. Doctor is a liability. #178359 and #187900 both report doctor hanging with no output across OSes — the intended recovery tool is itself unreliable, compounding incidents.
  3. Upgrade fragility. #169844, #164800, #187917, #183479, #169423, #157812: Windows Scheduled Task hangs, activation-driver death, retained-package blocks, codex-migration stalls. Multi-hop upgrades (#169423) are a real operational hazard.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — AI Agent / Personal AI Assistant Open-Source Ecosystem

Data window: 2026-11-02 → 2026-11-03 UTC | Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The five projects surveyed sit at different maturity points within a single converging category: persistent, multi-channel AI agents with tool execution, memory, and gateway-based orchestration. Activity is sharply bifurcated — OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw are all in post-migration or pre-release hardening phases (unified gateway regressions, v0.9.0 gating, 2.3.0 beta stabilization), while IronClaw is effectively dormant with only automated dependency churn. The dominant engineering cost across the ecosystem is no longer model capability but operational reliability: session durability, silent-failure diagnostics, and security boundary enforcement. Security auditing by community members is now a routine, line-cited activity in at least three projects, indicating the ecosystem is being deployed as real infrastructure rather than toy assistants. A consistent gap remains between contribution volume and maintainer review/merge capacity.

Hermes Agent has the highest absolute PR volume but is absorbing a large architectural migration. IronClaw's zero-human-activity window is the only true red flag in the set.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs peers

  • Largest absolute community and throughput — 391 issues / 500 PRs touched in 24h is ~8–10× Hermes or ZeroClaw on a per-window basis, and orders of magnitude above QwenPaw.
  • Most mature release discipline — the only project to ship a versioned release with documented security-hardening content (secret-redacted Git backups covering PostgreSQL and plugin credentials) in this window.
  • Broadest provider and channel surface — Databricks provider PR with sufficient proof (#155634), plus Telegram/WeChat/Matrix/Slack routing already in production use.
  • Explicit security culture at the issue level — P0 security tags (transcript redaction poisoning #142821, tools.fs.workspaceOnly bypass #173058) are tracked with severity labels rather than buried.

Where it is weaker than it looks

  • The stale-sweep closure pattern is a genuine risk: two security-relevant issues (#158966 CDP credential leakage, #161208 prompt-cache cost) were closed as stale, not fixed. This is a governance debt that peers (notably ZeroClaw's line-cited audit culture) handle better.
  • P0 blockers lack fix PRs (#166634 permanent UNAVAILABLE after crash recovery, #169844 Windows activation hang) — breadth of contributors is not translating to ownership of the hardest items.

Technical approach differences

  • OpenClaw leans on a rich plugin/extension model with bundled credentials and a native host-exec path (Direct shared-state reader, integrity admission errors) — heavier machinery than QwenPaw's Python/AgentScope stack or Hermes's gateway-centric design.
  • It is the only project in the set shipping a dedicated backup/restore subsystem with security review as a first-class release feature — a sign of enterprise-adjacent intent.

Community size comparison: OpenClaw ≫ Hermes ≈ ZeroClaw > QwenPaw ≫ IronClaw. The long tail of contributor handles (many drive-by docs/UI PRs) suggests OpenClaw has crossed into broad-contributor territory, whereas Hermes and ZeroClaw still show concentrated, repeat-contributor patterns.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

The following requirements recur across three or more projects, making them ecosystem-level rather than project-specific:

Session/turn durability across transport OpenClaw (#166634 crash-recovery), Hermes (#146344 admission_conflict, #145889 gateway wedge), ZeroClaw (#7759 turn/WS decoupling), QwenPaw (#8532 append-only session storage) Long-running turns must survive reloads, disconnects, restarts; append-only/checkpointed session state is emerging as the convergent design.

Cross-cutting root cause: Most "instability" reports are actually observability failures — the system is doing something (degraded fallback, silent skip, stale config) that the user cannot distinguish from a hang or a bug.

Architecture divergence note: Hermes and ZeroClaw both recently centralized on a gateway-based session admission model — and both are now paying a regression tax (admission conflicts, profile scope bleed, worker permission denials). OpenClaw uses a shared-state + integrity-admission model with a different failure class (checkpoint expiration, identity loss). QwenPaw is converging on append-only session storage, which if it lands cleanly may prove the most robust of the three designs — worth watching as a reference implementation.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Tier 1 — High-momentum, broad-contributor: OpenClaw. Largest absolute activity; production-scale contributor diversity; but momentum is partly artificial (stale sweeps) and P0 ownership is thin. Maturity is high on feature surface, medium on reliability.

Tier 2 — High-momentum, migration-stressed: Hermes Agent and ZeroClaw.

  • Hermes shows strong maintainer throughput and a highly engaged community functioning as a QA layer (47-comment triage). It is stabilizing after an architectural migration — v0.23.0 will be a stabilization release.
  • ZeroClaw is rapidly iterating toward a security+reliability v0.9.0 but is review-capacity-bound. Its community is the most security-literate in the set.

Tier 2b — High-momentum, disciplined closure: QwenPaw. Lower absolute volume than Tier 1/2, but the best issue-to-PR turnaround and cleanest closure ratio. In an active beta stabilization — most "bugs" are beta-testing surface, not architectural rot. Fastest path from report to fix in the cohort.

Tier 3 — Dormant: IronClaw. Zero human-authored activity; only automated dependency bumps. Stable and low-risk on security, but cannot be assessed as actively maintained from this window — monitor for return of human PRs before relying on it.

Maturity framing: Features-mature but reliability-immature (OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw) is the common pattern; QwenPaw is closest to balanced; IronClaw is maintenance-only. No project in the set has reached "reliability-mature."

7. Trend Signals (for AI Agent Developers)

Extracted from cross-project community feedback, ranked by signal strength:

  1. Reliability is the new differentiator — diagnostic opacity is the top complaint. Across all four active projects, the highest-engagement threads are diagnosability problems, not feature requests. Actionable: invest in invariant checks + surfaced error codes + progress observability (especially in long-running repair/doctor paths) before adding capabilities. "False-green health" is a trust-killer.

  2. Session/turn durability is the architectural battleground. Multiple projects are independently converging on append-only, checkpointed, transport-decoupled session state (ZeroClaw #7759, QwenPaw #8532, OpenClaw crash-recovery #166634). Actionable: design for turns that survive reload/restart/disconnect from day one; treat WS/socket lifetime as ephemeral.

  3. "Advertised ≠ enforced" is the dominant security failure mode. Config keys accepted but unread (ZeroClaw), default-on protections that poison data (OpenClaw), declared guards that don't gate (QwenPaw). Actionable: validate and enforce config at startup, fail loudly on unknown/unread keys, and audit that security switches actually run. Community security auditing (line-cited, reproducible) is now expected — build for it.

  4. BYO-provider correctness is a silent-data-loss class. Unknown models and missing context-window config silently fall back to wrong defaults (ZeroClaw 32k, QwenPaw max_tokens injection, OpenClaw cache non-reuse). Actionable: loud validation on model/provider config and explicit context-window contracts; do not assume.

  5. Cost observability is a first-class user need. Prompt-cache non-reuse, idle CPU/GPU burn (Hermes desktop 25–45%, OpenClaw Matrix E2EE ~50% CPU), heartbeat cache misses — users measure and resent infrastructure cost. Actionable: surface cache-hit rates, idle resource usage, and per-turn cost; treat cache stability as a feature (e.g., deferred MCP loading that busts cache, ZeroClaw #11703).

  6. Plugin/dependency isolation is an ecosystem-health prerequisite. Shared-dependency models cause cascading activation failures; catalog pinning and plugin CLI/extension points are emerging. Actionable: isolate plugin dependency environments, pin catalog entries, and expose resource lifecycle hooks — the plugin ecosystem is the moat, and fragility there blocks third-party growth.

  7. Windows and i18n are real, underserved segments. Consistent Windows-specific defect clusters and explicit non-English deployment demand (Hermes 17-language parity, QwenPaw Chinese-Windows data-loss fixes). Actionable: treat Windows and localization as first-class test targets, not afterthoughts — encoding (GBK/CP932/CRLF), path handling (UNC, Chinese paths), and packaging completeness.

  8. Maintainer review capacity, not contribution volume, is the ecosystem's bottleneck. OpenClaw's unowned P0s, ZeroClaw's stalled S1 fix PRs, QwenPaw's competing duplicate CRLF PRs all point the same way. Actionable for developers: file reproducible, line-cited reports (the ones getting fast turnaround share this trait); for maintainers: explicit triage SLAs on security-labeled issues and consolidation of duplicate fix efforts.

Bottom line for decision-makers: OpenClaw is the broadest and most production-ready on feature surface but carries unresolved reliability and stale-sweep security debt — adopt with a doctor-first upgrade discipline and independent verification of "closed-as-stale" security items. Hermes and ZeroClaw are stabilizing toward reliability releases and are the best bets for teams that prioritize security rigor and durable sessions, provided you can tolerate migration-phase friction. QwenPaw offers the best closure discipline and fastest fix cycles for channel/plugin-heavy and Chinese-Windows deployments. IronClaw should be treated as dormant until human-authored activity resumes. Across all: budget for observability and session durability as core engineering, not polish.

QwenPaw — agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

QwenPaw Project Digest — 2026-11-03

1. Today's Overview

QwenPaw shows high-velocity development activity with 18 issues and 37 PRs updated in the last 24 hours, indicating an engaged contributor base and active triage cycle. The project is currently in a 2.3.0 beta stabilization phase (v2.3.0-beta.1 through b3 referenced throughout), with numerous bug reports surfacing from beta testing—particularly around desktop builds, plugin dependency resolution, and channel integrations. Eleven PRs were merged or closed today, including fixes for the visual compression asset bundling issue (#8514, #8488) and CRLF/encoding preservation in file tools. However, no new releases were published, and several high-severity issues remain open, including a security governance gap (#8513) and a plugin activation blocker (#8553). Overall project health is good but watchful—the rapid issue-to-PR turnaround on most bugs suggests responsive maintainership, though the beta testing surface is exposing integration fragility across platform-specific paths.

2. Releases

None. No new releases were published in the last 24 hours.

3. Project Progress

Merged/Closed PRs today (11 total):

  • #8514 [CLOSED] — fix(desktop): bundle visual_compression glyph atlas assets — Fixes the PyInstaller build omission where agents/context/visual_compression/assets was not in _data_dirs, causing FileNotFoundError on desktop builds. Directly resolves Issue #8488. Link

  • #8556 [CLOSED] — fix(console): select decision-model approval directly — Simplifies the decision-model tool approval UX by removing the redundant "Use decision model" switch; selecting approval mode is now the sole opt-in. Link

  • #8463 [CLOSED] — feat(models): run local Piccolo with bidirectional candidate scoring — Enables downloaded Piccolo models to supply native Jev decisions for automatic tool review and ReMe context compaction, using bidirectional prompt attention rather than a causal Chat Completions adapter. Link

  • #8496 [CLOSED] — fix(context): support slow summary models and consistent token limits — Resolves HTTP 400 errors on OpenAI-compatible providers when model cards set generate_kwargs.max_tokens (AgentScope 2.0.10 injects max_completion_tokens while Scroll also passes max_tokens). Link

  • #8552 [CLOSED] — fix(tests): reopen backup archive before Windows restore verification — Test-only fix for Windows ZIP handle path separator mismatch (BadZipFile). Link

Also closed as issues (6 today): #8265 (plugin hot-install abort on importlib.invalidate_caches()), #8488 (desktop visual compression assets), #4312 (agent.json hot-reload scope), #8013 (skill pool download timeout), #8528 (Markdown preview relative path rewrite), #8540 (scroll history startup sync).

Key advancement: The edit_file CRLF/encoding preservation fix has two competing open PRs (#8235 and #8433), addressing Issues #8414 and #8415—this is an active hot-fix zone for Windows users.

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Comments Link Underlying Need
#8265 Plugin hot-install aborts (importlib.invalidate_caches raises) 5 Issue Plugin ecosystem reliability—users install third-party plugins and need robust, distro-agnostic loading. This was the most-discussed issue, now closed.
#8488 Desktop build omits visual_compression assets 3 Issue Packaging completeness—desktop users expect feature parity with source builds; missing assets silently break Visual Compact.
#8505 Gateway bare APIError classified as unknown (no retry/fallback) 3 Issue Resilience against OpenAI-compatible relays—users route through Chinese gateways that emit non-standard error shapes; model fallback is critical.
#8553 QQ channel plugin DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED (aliyun-hub) 2 Issue Shared dependency isolation—hub plugins without dependency environments block downstream consumers; activation audit is too strict.
#8511 Feishu channel intermittent No active model configured 2 Issue Concurrency correctness in channel message handling—race between inbound message and in-flight agent processing.
#8532 feat(chat): append-only session storage, paginated history, native Turn forks — PR Long-conversation scalability—durable per-session SQLite with append-only facts replacing mutable snapshots. XXXL-sized, under review.
#8554 feat(plugins): CLI commands and extension points — PR Plugin developer ergonomics—Click command registration, dependency checks, resource lifecycle hooks.

Analysis: The community is pushing on three fronts simultaneously: (1) plugin/channel integration reliability, (2) desktop distribution parity, and (3) long-session durability. The PR #8532 (append-only session storage) and #8554 (plugin CLI) are the highest-leverage architectural changes in flight.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

🔴 Critical — Security

  • #8513 [OPEN] — Shell-wrapped outbound actions execute with no findings or approval at AUTO/SMART — Detector gap in tool_guard AND governance lanes; SMTP send / HTTP POST / @file-to-network all pass ungated. This is an exfiltration risk under approval_level: AUTO. No fix PR yet. Issue

🟠 High — Data Loss / Corruption

  • #8414 [OPEN] — edit_file converts all CRLF to LF on targeted edit — Rewrites entire file newline style; Windows users lose line-ending contract. Fix PRs exist: #8235, #8433 (both under review, competing). Issue

  • #8549 [OPEN] — Model config write path bypasses field validation — Invalid thinking_budget/max_input_length persisted; provider silently disappears after restart. Fix PR #8550 open (first-time contributor). Issue

🟠 High — Instability

  • #8505 [OPEN] — Gateway bare APIError classified as unknown — No retry, no model fallback on HTTP 502 relays. No fix PR. Issue

  • #8553 [OPEN] — QQ channel DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED — Activation aborts when hub plugin (aliyun-hub) has no dependency environment. PR #8527 (dependency state root reporting) is related but not a direct fix. Issue

  • #8511 [OPEN] — Feishu channel No active model configured during concurrent processing — Reproduced on stable 2.2.2, not beta-introduced. Race condition. Issue

🟡 Medium — Platform/UX

  • #8555 [OPEN] — New task workspace selection reverts to default in subsequent messages (v2.3.0b3) Issue
  • #8517 [OPEN] — Hub Docker runtime Permission denied on working/config.json as non-root Issue
  • #8502 [OPEN] — Desktop HTML preview "Open in browser" fails on Chinese paths / out-of-workspace files — Fix PR #8524 open (decoded local path). Issue
  • #8547 [OPEN] — Creator: bundled cat-perspective example still cannot open on Windows (regression of #7291) Issue
  • #8534 [OPEN] — Creator: TTS cannot use Aliyun Token Plan key — qwen-audio-tts uses different DashScope service; protocol option missing from UI. Issue
  • #8533 [OPEN] — Codex/Qoder backend cron jobs misjudge non-empty requests as empty — ValueError: Third-party agent requests require text or attachments. Issue

Fix coverage: 4 of 10 open bugs have associated fix PRs (#8414→#8235/#8433, #8549→#8550, #8502→#8524, #8488→#8514 closed). The security issue #8513 has no fix PR and should be prioritized.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

In-flight feature PRs (likely next version):

  • #8532 [OPEN, XXXL] Append-only session storage + paginated history + native Turn forks — Major architectural change for long conversations. Strong candidate for 2.3.0 final or 2.4.0. PR
  • #8554 [OPEN, XXXL] Plugin CLI commands and extension points — Extends Click tree with register_cli(CliSpec(...)), dependency checks, resource lifecycle. Plugin ecosystem maturity. PR
  • #8557 [OPEN, M] Per-run sessions for cron jobs — Bounds cron history growth; currently every run appends to one dedicated per-job session with full history. PR
  • #8444 [OPEN, L] Jev completion decisions — Optional decision-model self-check to flag promised-but-undelivered work when text-only replies trigger qualitative rubrics. PR
  • #8599/#8581 [OPEN, S] Matrix E2EE dependencies installed by default + legacy state migration simplification — Matrix channel hardening. PR #8559
  • #8504 [OPEN, XXXL] Desktop approval notifications — Unified system notifications for approval requests, completions, background tasks even when app is backgrounded. Closes #8460. PR
  • #8434 [OPEN, S] Quick Add Model button on Models page — Reduces 5 interactions across 3 screens to a single action. Fixes #4036. PR
  • #8236 [OPEN, L] Ollama context window from num_ctx instead of 128k default — Local model accuracy fix. PR

Prediction: 2.3.0 final likely ships with session storage (#8532), plugin CLI (#8554), and the accumulated beta bug fixes. Matrix E2EE and desktop notifications may land in 2.4.0.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (verbatim themes):

  1. Plugin dependency fragility (#8265, #8553): "我的插件被这个卡了" ("my plugin is blocked by this") — users are hitting real-world distro backports and hub dependency audit failures. The shared-dependency model (dependency_mode: shared) creates cascading activation failures.

  2. Windows platform second-class citizenship (#8488, #8414, #8502, #8547, #8528, #8552): CRLF normalization, Chinese paths, GBK encoding, PyInstaller asset omission—6+ distinct Windows-specific defects reported or fixed today. PR #8234 (GBK/CP936 decode instead of dropping bytes) addresses a long-standing data-loss issue for Chinese Windows users.

  3. Silent failures (#8488, #8549, #8505): Visual Compact no-ops silently; model config accepts invalid values then provider vanishes; gateway 502 becomes unknown with no retry. Users want loud, actionable diagnostics.

  4. Third-party backend integration (#8533, #8534): Codex/Qoder cron jobs misjudge content; Aliyun Token Plan keys incompatible with TTS. Users are mixing providers aggressively and hitting seam failures.

  5. Channel concurrency (#8511): Feishu users get intermittent "Internal error" when sending while agent is busy—perceived as instability.

Satisfaction signals: High issue-to-PR velocity (multiple same-day fixes), first-time contributor engagement (#8550), and detailed bug reports with source-level analysis (#8517, #8414, #8505) suggest a technically sophisticated, invested user base. The security report #8513 is particularly well-researched and reflects a user doing responsible disclosure rather than complaining.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered / needing maintainer attention:

Item Age Why it matters
#8513 Security: outbound shell actions ungated at AUTO/SMART Created 2026-10-30, 1 comment No fix PR; exfiltration risk. Highest priority. Issue
#8235 / #8433 Competing CRLF edit_file fixes Both created 2026-10-14/26, under review Duplicate effort—maintainers should consolidate to avoid merge conflict and contributor frustration. PR #8235 · PR #8433
#8234 GBK/CP936 decode in read/edit/grep Created 2026-10-14, under review Data-loss fix for Chinese Windows; stalled 20 days. PR
#8236 Ollama num_ctx context sizing Created 2026-10-14, under review Local model accuracy; stalled 20 days. PR
#4312 agent.json hot-reload scope (MCP, Skills) Created 2026-05-14, closed today after 6 months Good closure, but indicates backlog depth—feature requests can languish months. Issue
#8013 Skill pool download timeout (12,994 files, 80MB) Created 2026-09-29, closed today Large-skill handling needed three-layer fix (frontend 30s abort, backend copy, final workspace landing). Issue

Recommendation: Maintainers should (1) assign #8513 to a security-capable contributor immediately, (2) pick one CRLF fix (#8235 or #8433) and close the other with credit, and (3) batch-review the three stalled 2026-10-14 PRs (#8234, #8235, #8236) from contributor Li-john1021 to retain engagement.

The unmet expectation: invalid or degraded config should fail loudly at startup, not mid-turn.
  • Long-running work must survive the transport. Multiple threads (#7759, #9562, #12107, #12208, #12209) trace back to users treating the web chat as a production console and being burned by reloads, disconnects, or auto-scroll stealing their scroll position — a clear sign of real daily use on mobile/flaky networks.
  • Power users are running multi-agent/multi-channel topologies. Matrix peer routing (#10926), send_message_to_peer autonomy bypass (#12167), and mid-turn steering (#10893) come from users operating agent groups, not single assistants.
  • Security reporters are doing careful, line-cited audits (#9394, #12050, #12052, #12126, #12127) — the community is treating ZeroClaw as a deployable daemon with real threat models (proxies, OIDC, Windows UNC), which is a sign of maturity but also of accumulated security debt.
  • Satisfaction signal: quick turnaround on web/chat UX fixes (same-day PRs #12208/#12209) suggests maintainers are responsive to the frontend pain points users surface most.

Items needing maintainer attention due to age, severity, or blocked status:

  • #9859 — Distroless image missing sh (S1, open since 2026-08-09, only 2 comments, 1 👍). Long-standing release-artifact blocker with no linked fix.
  • #11580 — x86_64 Linux binary ~0.7 MB under the 64 MiB cap; needs a recorded headroom policy decision (needs-maintainer-review, v0.9.0). A gate decision, not a coding task — ideal for a maintainer call this week.
  • #10893 — Steering pipeline exists but has no producer; status:blocked and unowned. Deserves a design decision or explicit deferral.
  • #9394 — Though fix PR #12213 is open, the issue has lingered since July with release:v0.9.0; reviewer capacity is the bottleneck.
  • #11272 — Release fix for missing dashboard embed in Linux/Windows desktop kernels, open since 2026-09-30 with no comments; if unmerged, shipped desktop builds are visibly broken.
  • #11456 — Subprocess memory watchdog, needs-maintainer-review, open since Oct 2; valuable for untrusted-shell safety but stalled.
  • #11052 — closed today ✅, listed only as a resolution note.

Bottom line: ZeroClaw is highly active and clearly converging on a security-and-reliability v0.9.0, but the open:closed issue ratio (24:1) and several stale S1 items (#9859, #11272) indicate that review/merge capacity, not contribution volume, is the project's current constraint.
